research.statement: For Z=q(S), the categorical score is E[S|Z] and I_q=Var(E[S|Z])=Σ_b W_b μ_b μ_b^T=Σ_b m_b m_b^T/W_b.
research.title: Quantized Fisher-information identity

research.statement: I_full-I_q=E[Cov(S|Z)] is positive semidefinite; hard quantization cannot increase Fisher information.
research.title: Exact Fisher-information loss decomposition

research.statement: d-tr(I_full^{-1}I_q)=E||z-E[z|Z]||^2 for z=I_full^{-1/2}s; maximizing retained normalized trace is weighted k-means.
research.title: Normalized trace equals Fisher-whitened k-means

research.statement: For every centroid μ_c, μ_c^T I^{-1}μ_c<=1/W_c, and for δ=μ_a-μ_b, δ^T I^{-1}δ<=1/W_a+1/W_b.
research.title: D leverage inequality

research.statement: For distinct positive-weight score atoms obtained by merging duplicate rows, positive-definite retained information, exactly K nonempty cells, no move constraints beyond preserving nonempty cells, and zero-tolerance exact stability, every tied-or-worse nearest-centroid comparison from a non-singleton source has strictly positive exact D gain. Stability forces distinct centroids; singleton rows are then strictly nearest to their own centroids. Hence one-point exchange stability implies strict self-consistent D-Voronoi geometry.
